# 1 Samuel Chapter 22 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 163 | **Source Images:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1SA_022_page_001.jpg, 1SA_022_page_002.jpg

---

**1** And David departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam. And when his brothers and all the house of his father heard of it, they went down to him there.

**2** And every man who was in distress, and every man who was in debt, and every man who was bitter of soul gathered to him. And he became commander over them, and there were with him about four hundred men.

**3** And David went from there to Mizpeh of Moab. And he said to the king of Moab, "Please let my father and my mother come out to be with you, until I know what God will do for me."

**4** And he led them before the king of Moab, and they dwelt with him all the time that David was in the stronghold.

**5** And the prophet Gad said to David, "Do not remain in the stronghold. Go and enter the land of Judah." And David departed and came into the forest of Hereth.

**6** And Saul heard that David and the men who were with him had been discovered. Now Saul was sitting in Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the height, with his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing around him.

**7** And Saul said to his servants who were standing around him, "Hear now, O Benjaminites! Will the son of Jesse also give to all of you fields and vineyards? Will he make all of you commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?

**8** For all of you have conspired against me, and there is no one who discloses to my ear when my son makes a covenant with the son of Jesse. And there is none of you who is grieved over me or discloses to my ear that my son has stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as at this day."

**9** And Doeg the Edomite, who was standing among the servants of Saul, answered and said, "I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.

**10** And he inquired of the LORD for him and gave him provisions, and the sword of Goliath the Philistine he gave to him."

**11** And the king sent to summon Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, the priest, and all the house of his father, the priests who were in Nob. And all of them came to the king.

**12** And Saul said, "Hear now, son of Ahitub." And he said, "Here I am, my lord."

**13** And Saul said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the son of Jesse, in that you gave him bread and a sword, and inquired of God for him, so that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?"

**14** And Ahimelech answered the king and said, "And who among all your servants is as faithful as David, who is the son-in-law of the king, and captain over your bodyguard, and honored in your house?

**15** Did I begin today to inquire of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king impute anything to his servant, or to all the house of my father, for your servant knew nothing of all this, small or great."

**16** And the king said, "You shall surely die, Ahimelech — you, and all the house of your father."

**17** And the king said to the runners who stood about him, "Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because their hand also is with David, and because they knew that he fled and did not disclose it to my ear." But the servants of the king were not willing to stretch out their hand to strike the priests of the LORD.

**18** And the king said to Doeg, "You turn and strike the priests." And Doeg the Edomite turned and he struck the priests. And he killed on that day eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.

**19** And Nob, the city of the priests, he struck with the edge of the sword — both men and women, children and infants, and oxen and donkeys and sheep — with the edge of the sword.

**20** And one son of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub escaped, and his name was Abiathar. And he fled after David.

**21** And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.

**22** And David said to Abiathar, "I knew on that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul. I have brought about the death of every person of the house of your father.

**23** Stay with me; do not be afraid, for whoever seeks my soul seeks your soul, for you are under protection with me."

---

## LOGOS Translation Notes

Chapter 22 contains two distinct movements: the gathering of David's outcast band (vv. 1-5) and the massacre at Nob (vv. 6-23). The chapter opens with the same verse that closes chapter 21 in the MT tradition (21:16 // 22:1) — this translation follows the standard English verse division.

In verse 2, the phrase מַר־נֶפֶשׁ (mar-nefesh) is rendered "bitter of soul" in keeping with the convention for nefesh. The term מְצוּדָה (metsudah, "stronghold") in verses 4-5 likely refers to a fortified position, possibly Masada or another Judean wilderness refuge.

Verse 8 reveals Saul's paranoia through the repeated phrase "discloses to my ear" (גֹּלֶה אֶת־אָזְנִי, goleh et-ozni), literally "uncovers my ear." In verse 17, the term רָצִים (ratsim, "runners") designates the royal guard; their refusal to strike the priests contrasts sharply with Doeg's willingness (v. 18). The number eighty-five (חמשׁה ושׁמנים) priests slaughtered constitutes a near-total annihilation of the Elide priesthood, fulfilling the oracle of 1 Samuel 2:31-33.

Verse 23 concludes with David's solemn assumption of responsibility — מִשְׁמֶרֶת (mishmeret) rendered "protection" carries the sense of guarded keeping.

— LOGOS (Λόγος), translated from the Leningrad Codex (B19A)
